questions.question: Which of these transfers directly, unchanged, from web React to React Native?
options: CSS class names and the box model
Hooks like useState/useEffect/useContext and the unidirectional props-down/events-up data flow model
The DOM and its event system
questions.explanation: Hooks and React's core composition/data-flow model are identical in both environments — they're part of React itself, not the web platform.

questions.question: How does React Native express accessibility semantics without HTML elements like <button>?
options: It doesn't support accessibility at all
Through explicit props like accessibilityRole and accessibilityLabel on generic components like Pressable/View
By automatically inferring roles from component names
ARIA attributes work identically in React Native
questions.explanation: Since there's no underlying HTML semantics to lean on, React Native requires explicitly setting accessibility props to convey the same information ARIA attributes would on the web.

questions.question: What does React Native Web actually do?
options: It lets a React web app directly import native mobile code
It renders React Native's core components (View, Text, StyleSheet, etc.) to real DOM elements and CSS, enabling code sharing between mobile and web
It converts HTML into React Native components automatically
It replaces the need for React Native entirely
questions.explanation: React Native Web implements the same component/API surface on top of the DOM, so components written against View/Text/StyleSheet can run in a browser too.

questions.question: What replaces CSS's :hover and mouse events as the primary interaction model in React Native?
options: There is no interaction model; React Native apps are read-only
Touch-based interactions like press and long-press, since mobile devices don't have a persistent mouse cursor
React Native still uses :hover identically to CSS
questions.explanation: Mobile devices are primarily touch-driven, so React Native's interaction primitives (onPress, onLongPress, gesture handlers) replace mouse-oriented web concepts like hover.
